slot.brief: Two bodies collide and stick together (e.g., a moving body hits a resting one); apply momentum conservation to find the common velocity and then the kinetic energy lost in the collision.

stem: A $2\ \text{kg}$ block moving at $8\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ collides with a stationary $6\ \text{kg}$ block on a smooth surface, and they stick together. How much kinetic energy is lost in the collision?

verdicts.working: By momentum conservation, the combined speed is \(v=(2\times8)/8=2\,\text{m s}^{-1}\). Initial KE = 64 J; final KE = 16 J, so the loss is 48 J.

working:
$v=\dfrac{2(8)}{2+6}=2\ \text{m s}^{-1}$; $K_i=\dfrac{1}{2}(2)(8^2)=64\ \text{J}$; $K_f=\dfrac{1}{2}(8)(2^2)=16\ \text{J}$; $\Delta K=48\ \text{J}$

Independent check: By momentum conservation, the combined speed is \(v=(2\times8)/8=2\,\text{m s}^{-1}\). Initial KE = 64 J; final KE = 16 J, so the loss is 48 J.
solution:
By conservation of momentum, the common speed after collision is
$$v=\frac{(2)(8)}{2+6}=2\ \text{m s}^{-1}.$$
The kinetic energy lost is $K_i-K_f=\frac12(2)(8^2)-\frac12(8)(2^2)=64-16=48\ \text{J}$.
